text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Volkswagen's Bratislava plant has launched a new assembly line for the Passat B5 model. The company plans to complete some 4,000 units this year.

- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) has acussed other opposition parties and President Michal Kovac of taking part in thwarting referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last month.
- The strongest opposition parties, the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) and the Democratic Union (DU), have both rejected any talks with Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

- Local money and forex markets remained paralyzed last week and showed little trading activity as the central bank continued its strategy of keeping the markets short of crown liquidity to prevent pressure on the currency.
SME - SDL said it would propose its own draft law on direct presidential elections at the next parliamentary session.
- SDL has repeatedly said it is against early elections.

- The state Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting is expected to announce in the near future the winner of the tender for privatisating Slovak Television's second terrestrial channel (STV 2). The winner will then have to be approved by parliament.
- Opposition parties have proposed a law that should bar privatisation of STV 2.

PRAVDA - The positive ruling of the Constitutional Court on whether the constitution can be changed by a referendum showed that state authorities have breached the constitution by withdrawing a question on direct presidential elections from ballots at the recent NATO and presidential elections plebiscites.
- Slovakia's largest distributor of motor fuels, Benzinol a.s., plans to invest more than one billion crowns into the reconstruction of its local petrol stations this year.
- Bratislava's public transport company trade unions have called a drivers's strike on June 3.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's sole producer of tobacco prducts, SIT a.s., posted a net profit of 113.9 million crowns in 1996, on an overall turnover of 3.8 billion crowns.

- President Michal Kovac has returned a controversial law on the so-called revitalisation of ailing state enterprises to parliament for reassesment. Kovac argued the law was in contradiction with free market principles and the consitution.
